h2: NDT program management: running the program, not only writing it
html:
Many US and Canadian NDT companies do not need a Level III for a single document; they need someone to keep the whole program running. NDT program management is the name for that ongoing work: the written practice stays current, procedures are approved before they are used, examinations are written and graded properly, certification files are complete, and the company is ready for a client or registrar audit at any time.

What an outsourced Level III manages

  • Written practice upkeep: revisions when SNT-TC-1A, CP-189 or a client specification changes, and when the company adds a method.
  • Procedures and technique sheets: writing, reviewing and approving them for each code and client; see NDT procedure writing.
  • Examinations: preparing and grading general, specific and practical examinations, and keeping the question banks under control.
  • Certification files: checking training and experience hours, vision examinations and expiry dates before each certification is signed.
  • Audits: an internal audit before the external one, and support during client, registrar and owner audits; see NDT auditing services.
  • Technical questions: technique choice, interpretation of acceptance criteria and disputed indications.

Level III retainer or project

A Level III retainer suits companies that need these tasks every month: the Level III is named in the written practice and the work is planned across the year. A project suits a single deliverable, such as a new written practice or a set of procedures. Both are scoped and quoted on request, and the ASNT Level III consulting page explains how a named outside Level III works with your team.

NDT training and Level III consulting together

Programs most often fail where training and certification meet: training hours that are not documented the way the written practice says, or examinations that do not match the course. Because Atlantis NDT provides both NDT training and Level III consulting, course records, examinations and certification files can be designed as one system. Technicians train through NDT training courses, the company's records sit in the certification register, and the Level III signs against evidence that already matches the written practice.

Where to start

If you are unsure what your program needs, start with a review of the current written practice and a sample of certification files; the written practice development page shows what a complete one contains. Request a confidential technical discussion.
